outliers.name: Brian Braddock
outliers.verdict: Captain Britain: a British publishing history (Captain Britain Weekly, Excalibur, MI: 13), fame made outside this network

outliers.name: Miracleman (character)
outliers.verdict: Marvelman, a British character from 1954: four publishers and a 15-year legal fight over who owns him; almost none of it involves other Marvel heroes

outliers.name: Betsy Braddock
outliers.verdict: Psylocke: decades of X-Men plot, Captain Britain's twin, a 1989 redesign in a new body, and a reception section of fan polls

outliers.name: U.S. Agent
outliers.verdict: a replacement Captain America whose plot runs through nearly twenty storyline sections, from Force Works to the Thunderbolts; on screen since 2021

outliers.name: Quasar (character)
outliers.verdict: one title held by several characters; the in-links point at the name, the stories live on the holders' own pages

outliers.name: Blue Bullet
outliers.verdict: an Invaders villain with two appearances (1976 and 1993): little to say, and the page says little

outliers.name: Ch'od
outliers.verdict: a Starjammers alien in the X-Men books since 1977: often mentioned, rarely the subject

sentences.name: Spider-Man
sentences.text: Created by writer-editor Stan Lee and artist Steve Ditko, he first appeared in the anthology comic book Amazing Fantasy #15 (August 1962) in the Silver Age of Comic Books.

sentences.name: Hulk
sentences.text: Lee stated that the Hulk's creation was inspired by a combination of Frankenstein and Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde.

sentences.name: Wolverine (character)
sentences.text: The character first appeared in the comic book The Incredible Hulk #180 (1974) and is best known as a member of the superhero team the X-Men.

sentences.name: Doctor Strange
sentences.text: Created by artist Steve Ditko with scripting by Stan Lee, the character first appeared in Strange Tales #110 (cover-dated July 1963).

sentences.name: Deadpool
sentences.text: Created by artist Rob Liefeld and writer Fabian Nicieza, the character first appeared as a supervillain in The New Mutants #98 (cover dated February 1991) before recurring throughout X-Force and receiving his first miniseries, The Circle Chase, in 1993.

sentences.name: She-Hulk
sentences.text: Created by writer Stan Lee and artist John Buscema, she first appeared in The Savage She-Hulk #1 (November 1979).

sentences.name: Scarlet Witch
sentences.text: Created by writer Stan Lee and artist Jack Kirby, the character first appeared in The X-Men #4 (March 1964), in the Silver Age of Comic Books.

sentences.name: Black Panther (character)
sentences.text: Created by writer-editor Stan Lee and artist Jack Kirby, the character first appeared in Fantastic Four #52 (July 1966).

sentences.name: Cyclops (Marvel Comics)
sentences.text: Created by writer Stan Lee and artist/co-plotter Jack Kirby, the character first appeared in The X-Men #1 (cover dated September 1963) as a founding member of the X-Men.

sentences.name: Luke Cage
sentences.text: Created by Archie Goodwin, George Tuska, Roy Thomas, and John Romita Sr. in 1972, he was the first African-American superhero by Marvel Comics to be the main character in his own series.

sentences.name: Hank Pym
sentences.text: Created by penciller Jack Kirby, editor-plotter Stan Lee and writer Larry Lieber, Pym debuted in Tales to Astonish #27 (January 1962).

sentences.name: Phoenix (Guardians of the Galaxy)
sentences.text: Created by Chris Claremont and Dave Cockrum, the Phoenix Force is famous for its central role in The Dark Phoenix Saga storyline, and is intrinsically linked to Jean Grey.

sentences.name: Quasar (character)
sentences.text: They are noted for having worn the Quantum Bands, advanced ancient alien technology that grants the wearer manipulation of quantum energy.

sentences.name: Jean Grey
sentences.text: Created by writer Stan Lee and artist/co-plotter Jack Kirby, the character first appeared in The X-Men #1 (September 1963).

sentences.name: Moon Knight
sentences.text: Moon Knight is typically portrayed as a street-level vigilante with minimal superhuman abilities, relying instead on his athletic conditioning, expert hand-to-hand combat training, and detective skills to fight crime.

sentences.name: Black Widow (Natasha Romanova)
sentences.text: She reformed into a hero in The Avengers #30 (1966) and her most well-known design was introduced in The Amazing Spider-Man #86 (1970).

sentences.name: Iron Fist (character)
sentences.text: This ability is obtained from the city of K'un-L'un, which appears on Earth every 10 years.

sentences.name: Black Cat (Marvel Comics)
sentences.text: Created by Marv Wolfman and Dave Cockrum, the character first appeared in The Amazing Spider-Man #194 in July 1979 as an adversary of the superhero Spider-Man, although she later becomes his on-off love interest and ally.

sentences.name: Cable (character)
sentences.text: Born in the present-day, Nathan was infected with a deadly techno-organic virus as an infant and was sent into a possible future timeline where his condition could be stabilized.

sentences.name: Emma Frost
sentences.text: Created by writer Chris Claremont and artist/co-writer John Byrne, the character first appeared in The Uncanny X-Men #129 (January 1980).

sentences.name: Storm (Marvel Comics)
sentences.text: Created by writer Len Wein and artist Dave Cockrum, the character first appeared in Giant-Size X-Men #1 (May 1975).

sentences.name: Hercules (Marvel Comics)
sentences.text: Debuting in the Silver Age of Comic Books, the character is based on Heracles of Greek mythology (despite using the name of his Roman equivalent, Hercules).

sentences.name: Venom (character)
sentences.text: The character is a sentient alien symbiote with an amorphous, liquid-like form, who survives by bonding with a host, usually human.

sentences.name: Deathlok
sentences.text: The first Deathlok, Luther Manning, appeared in Astonishing Tales #25 (Aug. 1974), created by Rich Buckler.

sentences.name: Blade (character)
sentences.text: Shortly after his introduction, Blade became one of Marvel's most prominent supernatural heroes, appearing alongside teams including the Nightstalkers, the Midnight Sons, and the Avengers.

sentences.name: Human Torch
sentences.text: "Flame on!", which the Torch customarily shouts when activating his full-body flame effect, has become his catchphrase.

sentences.name: Nova (Richard Rider)
sentences.text: The character appeared historically as the star of his own series, and at other times, as a supporting character in team books such as The New Warriors.

sentences.name: Spider-Woman (Jessica Drew)
sentences.text: Bendis then added Spider-Woman to the roster of the New Avengers, which leads to her involvement in the "Secret Invasion" storyline.

sentences.name: Rachel Summers
sentences.text: The character was created by writer Chris Claremont and artist/co-plotter John Byrne.

sentences.name: Misty Knight
sentences.text: After receiving a bionic prosthetic from Tony Stark, she started a private-investigation agency with a close friend, Colleen Wing.

sentences.name: Man-Thing
sentences.text: Steve Gerber's 39-issue run on the series is considered to be a cult classic.

sentences.name: Human Torch (android)
sentences.text: Created by writer and artist Carl Burgos, he first appeared in Marvel Comics #1 (October 1939), published by Marvel's predecessor, Timely Comics.

sentences.name: Mayday Parker
sentences.text: The character was created by Tom DeFalco and Ron Frenz as the teenage daughter of Peter Parker (Spider-Man) and Mary Jane Watson, and first appeared in What If #105 (February 1998).

sentences.name: Shang-Chi
sentences.text: Marvel had originally hoped to license the television series Kung Fu, but the rights were unavailable, and the character was instead spun off from novelist Sax Rohmer's licensed pulp villain Fu Manchu as his previously unknown son.

sentences.name: Mockingbird (Marvel Comics)
sentences.text: The character first appeared in Astonishing Tales #6 in 1971 as a supporting character and eventual love interest of Ka-Zar, with a Ph.D. in biology.

sentences.name: Franklin Richards (character)
sentences.text: Franklin is an immensely powerful being with vast reality-manipulating and psionic powers beyond most Omega level mutants.

sentences.name: Ghost Rider
sentences.text: The first supernatural Ghost Rider is stunt motorcyclist Johnny Blaze, who agrees to give his soul to "Satan" (later revealed to be an arch-demon named Mephisto) to save the life of his foster father.

sentences.name: Black Bolt
sentences.text: Black Bolt's signature power is his voice, as his electron-harnessing ability is linked to the speech center of his brain.

sentences.name: Jericho Drumm
sentences.text: He first appeared in Strange Tales #169 (September 1973) as Brother Voodoo.

sentences.name: War Machine
sentences.text: Col. James Rupert "Rhodey" Rhodes is a military veteran and pilot who began working for Tony Stark, eventually discovering that he was Iron Man and then taking Stark's place when he was incapacitated.
